name: infra_ignite
title: PyTorch-Ignite: create_supervised_trainer / _evaluator, handlers, Checkpoint
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-infra: the Ignite script the ROADMAP's framework list names
note: A precision trap. Ignite's Engine owns the update step and the evaluator runs the model in eval mode under torch.no_grad(); every absence rule must stay silent, and it does. The graph half is the finding: `eval` and `deliver` are reported ABSENT on a file that builds an evaluator (line 70), runs it every epoch (line 77) and attaches a Checkpoint/DiskSaver handler (line 90). See the domain-infra report, finding INFRA-04.
stagesObserved: config, data, model, objective, train present; preprocess, eval and deliver reported absent.

forbidden.why: the training loader is built with shuffle=True at line 51
the validation loader is built with shuffle=False at line 53
no DataLoader in this file passes num_workers, so no worker process is spawned
create_supervised_trainer builds the update step (zero_grad, forward, loss, backward, step) itself; there is no hand-written batch loop in this file
same: the step lives inside the Engine Ignite returned
create_supervised_evaluator switches the model to eval() for the duration of its run
create_supervised_evaluator runs its inference step under torch.no_grad()
device= is passed to both create_supervised_trainer (line 67) and create_supervised_evaluator (line 70), and Ignite moves each batch with convert_tensor
the device is chosen behind torch.cuda.is_available() at line 59
ignite.utils.manual_seed(SEED) is called at line 58 and the random_split takes an explicit generator at line 50
SignalNet.__init__ calls super().__init__() as its first statement at line 30
every submodule is held by nn.Sequential or assigned directly; there is no plain list of modules
checkpointing goes through ignite.handlers.Checkpoint with a DiskSaver, not torch.save of a module, and this file never calls torch.load
